raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Hybrid attention/mamba models cannot use `--attention-backend b12x`: hybrid page alignment raises the KV block size above 128 (2176 in #62320), and b12x only accepted exactly 64 or 128. The worker already splits large manager blocks into the kernel page sizes a backend declares, and b12x declares 64 and 128, so this drops b12x's exact-size override and lets the standard split apply. Fixes #62320.

## Claims

- Hybrid models now start with `--attention-backend b12x`: the manager block is aligned to the mamba page (a multiple of 128) and the worker hands b12x 128-token kernel pages. `ValueError: Aligned KV cache block size ... is not supported by attention backend(s): B12X` is gone.
- Non-hybrid models are unaffected: with `--block-size` unset or 64/128 nothing changes; block sizes that are not a multiple of 64 are still rejected at selection.
- One override removed, one unit test added. No kernel or runner changes.

## Validation

DGX Spark (GB10, sm_121, aarch64), CUDA 13.0, torch 2.14.0+cu132, flashinfer-python 0.7.2 (provides the `b12x` module), vLLM main @ f98ae6a9f.

Reproducer close to #62320 (same Qwen3.5 GDN + full-attention layout, head_dim 256, 2 KV heads, under 1B parameters):

```python
from vllm import LLM
LLM("Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B", attention_config={"backend": "B12X"}, block_size=128, dtype="bfloat16")
```

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| startup | `Setting attention block size to 640 tokens ...` then `ValueError: Aligned KV cache block size 640 is not supported by attention backend(s): B12X.` | starts; manager block 640, b12x runs on 128-token kernel pages (`planned_page_sizes=(64, 128)`); generates |

Greedy outputs, b12x vs FLASH_ATTN on the same model: identical on 11 of 12 outputs (4 short prompts, a 300-token prompt, a 3k-token prompt spanning several aligned blocks, and a mixed batch of all six). The one that differs is a prompt whose greedy continuation also flips between two identical FLASH_ATTN runs on this model, i.e. a near-tie, not a kernel difference. Repeated b12x batches are identical.

Also tried `tiiuae/Falcon-H1-0.5B-Instruct` (Mamba2 hybrid, head_dim 64): with this change the aligned block of 896 is accepted and the engine proceeds to CUDA-graph capture, where the b12x kernel planner raises `no valid NUM_MMA_KV typed shared-memory allocation fits the device`. That is a head_dim 64 limitation of the b12x package (a non-hybrid head_dim 64 model, Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct, fails identically with `block_size=128`), independent of this PR; I will file it separately.

```
$ pytest tests/v1/attention/test_b12x.py
41 passed in 34.60s   # DGX Spark, GB10; includes the new test
```

The new test fails on main (`supports_block_size(2176)` is False there) and passes with this change. `pre-commit run --files ...` is clean.

## Details

`Platform._align_hybrid_block_size()` sets the manager block so one attention page is at least one mamba state page, rounded to the backend's kernel block alignment. For b12x that is a multiple of 128. `_check_aligned_block_size()` (#58457) then asks every backend `supports_block_size(aligned)`, and b12x's override answered False for anything but exactly 64 or 128.

The base `AttentionBackend.supports_block_size()` accepts any multiple of a declared kernel size for exactly this case ("the framework-level block size only needs to be a multiple of the kernel's requirement"). At runtime `prepare_kernel_block_sizes()` / `select_common_block_size()` pick the largest declared size that divides the manager block (128 for 2176), the KV cache is allocated in kernel pages, and `AttentionGroup.map_to_kernel_block_table()` expands the block table. b12x already reads the page size from the cache tensors (`_kv_page_size`), prepares plans for both page sizes, and sizes its page table for the hybrid expansion (`_max_page_table_width(..., is_hybrid)` adds the trailing capacity for exactly this split). So the only thing standing between hybrid models and b12x was the override.

`get_preferred_block_size()` is kept, so a non-hybrid model with no `--block-size` still gets 128 rather than the base class's minimum of 64 (with #62265).

Related: #62265 removes the same backend's constructor-time block-size check; this PR is independent of it when `--block-size` is passed explicitly (as in the report), and together they make `--attention-backend b12x` work for hybrid models with no `--block-size` at all.

Not a duplicate: no PR references #62320; the open b12x PRs (#54976, #54669, #54719, #55405) are about MoE/MLA selection.

I found this via #62320, which mentions my earlier b12x fix. I used Claude Code to Understand the split mechanism, traced it, and run the validation; I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests myself.

🚀

Deployment validation (SM120, hybrid attention/mamba) — the confirmation you asked for on #62320:

- **Model:** `Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B` (Qwen3.5-MoE — full-attention + GDN linear-attention layers, i.e. hybrid), NVFP4, TP=1, RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell SE (SM120)
- **Stack:** vLLM 0.32.0 + b12x 1.5.1 (the tag's `[b12x]` pin), full production flags: `--attention-backend b12x --linear-backend b12x --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 128 --enable-prefix-caching --max-model-len 262144 --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'`
- **Before this change:** startup fails with `ValueError: Aligned KV cache block size 2176 is not supported by attention backend(s): B12X` (#62320)
- **With this change:** the gate passes (`Setting attention block size to 2176`, no ValueError), b12x runs on 128-token kernel pages, and the full startup + check + 19-case functional bench pass (0 failures)

One caveat: our run additionally needed the `hasattr(binding.q, "fake_mode")` guard in b12x 1.5.1's paged-priming compile — the standalone wheel (what `vllm[b12x]` pins) predates that fix, which is on flashinfer `main` and in the FlashInfer 0.7.2 bundled b12x. It's a separate bug from this change (we carried the guard as a local image patch, version-pinned + fail-loud); tracked at flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6940.

So from our side: this change alone makes hybrid + b12x startable on 0.32.0 under the full production config (fp8 KV + MTP spec decode + prefix caching + chunked prefill, 2176 aligned block) — which goes beyond the PR's bf16 / DGX-Spark validation.

Thanks @mike2307, that's exactly the confirmation this needed: fp8 KV + MTP + prefix caching + chunked prefill on the 2176-token block, beyond what I could cover on the Spark. The fake_mode crash is in the standalone b12x 1.5.1 wheel and is tracked separately in #62984 / flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6940.

Thanks @waynehacking8, that closes the loop: same quality and decode throughput as the default backend on the 2176-token block, on hardware I can’t test. The 2176 vs 2112 difference is just each backend’s kernel alignment (128 for b12x, 16/32 for FlashInfer). The per-batch-size Triton compile in the b12x warmup is independent of this change (graph_replay metadata kernel with BATCH as a constexpr, driven by cutedsl_warmup over every capture size); I’ll check whether it’s tracked and file it if not.

@waynehacking8 filed the warmup compile issue you ran into as [flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#7030](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/7030), with your gist linked. It’s a tl.static_range(0, BATCH) in the b12x prefill metadata kernel, one unrolled compile per batch size; on my Spark a one-line range swap took the 128-seq warmup from 17 min to 19 s with identical outputs.

One thing my review left out: in the same runs b12x is slower to the first token. At c=1 the median TTFT is 90.1 ms against 79.2 ms for the default backend, over 16 requests each with a standard deviation of about 2 ms. At c=16 the medians (349.5 and 335.6 ms) differ by much less than the request-to-request spread (standard deviation 52 and 58 ms). The b12x server also needed 205 s to become ready against 140 s.

Both arms run this head with one boot each, so this compares the two backends, not the change. I've added these rows to the review table. Numbers: `P-b12x-c1.txt`, `P-def-c1.txt`, the two c=16 files and `job-log-run3.txt` in https://gist.github.com/waynehacking8/f77c201b8e02452ee5508a31162235bb

Thanks for adding those. Agreed it’s backend vs backend: this PR only lifts the block-size gate so b12x can start on hybrid models, and the hybrid split doesn’t touch the prefill path, so the c=1 TTFT gap is b12x’s own prefill cost on that card. Worth a separate look. The extra startup time is at least partly the per-batch warmup compile in [flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#7030](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/7030).

@LucasWilkinson @MatthewBonanni gentle ping on this one when you have a moment. It is a one-line change (drops the exact-size `supports_block_size` override so the worker's kernel-page split applies to b12x like the other backends), and since opening it has been confirmed independently on two SM120 setups above: mike2307 on Ornith-1.5-35B NVFP4 with fp8 KV, MTP and prefix caching, and waynehacking8 on Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-FP8 with GSM8K and TPOT matching the default FlashInfer path. Still applies cleanly to main. Happy to adjust if you would like it done differently.

Thanks @arpera for merging #62265! Since this one touches the same b12x block size code and the block 192 case came out of your review, it might make sense to look at the two together while it's still fresh. I tried merging current main with #62265 in locally and got no conflicts.

No rush at all, and I can run `/ci run` again whenever it's useful since the last build is from yesterday. @stecasta let me know if you'd like anything else changed here.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

Adding quality and speed to mike2307's startup and functional check: on an RTX PRO 6000 Max-Q (SM120) with Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-FP8, this diff (head dca790ae9a) on main a9bf45ed8a with `--attention-backend b12x --block-size 128` matches the default backend on GSM8K and c=16 decode, c=1 TPOT is 3% lower and c=1 TTFT is 14% higher, from one run per cell (main stops with the #62320 error here).

| metric (both on this head) | b12x | default (FlashInfer) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| aligned block size | 2176 | 2112 |
| GSM8K 200, greedy, no thinking | 0.445 | 0.435 |
| c=1 median TTFT, ms | 90.1 | 79.2 |
| c=1 median TPOT, ms | 4.32 | 4.46 |
| c=1 output tok/s | 209.6 | 206.0 |
| c=16 median TTFT, ms | 349.5 | 335.6 |
| c=16 median TPOT, ms | 9.88 | 9.88 |
| c=16 output tok/s | 1368.5 | 1370.1 |
| server ready after, s | 205 | 140 |

GSM8K here gets direct answers (7.6 output tokens on average), so it mostly checks prefill; 7 items are right only with b12x and 5 only with the default. The speed rows use 1000 random input tokens and 190 output tokens. TTFT varies between requests by about 2 ms at c=1 and 55 ms at c=16, so only the c=1 TTFT gap stands out.

All cells ran with `--max-num-seqs 32`. At this card's default of 1024, the b12x warmup (FlashInfer 0.7.2's bundled b12x) compiles a Triton metadata kernel once per batch size, and it was still compiling batch 149 about 16 minutes into that warmup. Setup: fp8 KV cache, prefix caching, max model length 32768, one server per cell, card otherwise idle. Logs and scripts: https://gist.github.com/waynehacking8/f77c201b8e02452ee5508a31162235bb

Hi @VidyasagarDudekula, LGTM. With the override gone, b12x uses the base `supports_block_size` like the other backends that declare fixed kernel sizes, and the hybrid runs above cover the 2176-token block on SM120.

Hi @VidyasagarDudekula, @arpera's review flagged an issue when this lands together with #62265, and the code trace confirms it, details inline. Could you check `--block-size 192` on your Spark before the next push?

Together with #62265, this lets a non-hybrid model run with an explicit block size that is a multiple of 64 but not 64 or 128. Example: Qwen3-0.6B, `block_size=192`, `max_model_len=4096`. The worker block table is `ceil(4096/192) = 22` blocks, which expands to 66 entries of 64-token kernel pages, but `_max_page_table_width()` (L62) sizes the plans for `ceil(4096/64) = 64`, and the extra capacity is only added for hybrid models. `forward()` passes the full table, so FlashInfer's check should reject it (`page_table width must fit the prepared capacity: got 66, expected 1..64`).

Should we size the plans from the manager block expanded into kernel pages, or keep rejecting sizes other than 64/128 for non-hybrid models? A test that the expanded table fits the plan would cover it.

Thanks, good catch. Reproduced on the Spark with both PRs applied (Qwen3-0.6B, `--block-size 192`, `--max-model-len 4096`): the engine dies at the first forward with `page_table width=66 exceeds scratch capacity 64` from `_scratch.py:_validate_runtime_metadata_reference` (a different check than the decode-graph one, same cause).

I went with sizing the plans from the manager block. `_max_page_table_width()` now takes the manager block size and mirrors what the worker does in `AttentionGroup.create_metadata_builders`: `get_block_table_width(cdiv(max_model_len, block_size), block_size) * (block_size // page_size)`. When the block is not known yet (the platform applies `get_preferred_block_size()` after the model is built) or is not a multiple of the page, it sizes for whole pages as before. The hybrid slack is unchanged.

Reusing `get_block_table_width` also covers the worker's 128-token block-table alignment: with `--block-size 64 --max-model-len 4000` the worker passes 64 entries but the plans were sized for `cdiv(4000, 64) = 63`. That one is independent of the two PRs (block size 64 passes both checks) and fails without them too: `page_table width=64 exceeds scratch capacity 63`.

Tests: `test_b12x_attention_plan_capacity_fits_expanded_block_table` sweeps block sizes 64..2176 and model lengths 1000..40960 and asserts the expanded worker table fits the plan, plus the two examples above; the new tests fail without the fix. On the Spark: `--block-size 192` and `--block-size 64 --max-model-len 4000` now start, greedy outputs match the 128 default, and the full `tests/v1/attention/test_b12x.py` passes (67 passed).

The new line sits a dozen lines below the constructor check #62265 removes, so the two should merge cleanly in either order.

Hi @VidyasagarDudekula, thanks for the quick fix. Sizing from the manager block through `get_block_table_width` matches what `create_metadata_builders` hands the backend, and the sweep test covers the 192 and 4000 cases. One merge issue with #62265 inline, otherwise LGTM.

#62265 deletes `cache_config = vllm_config.cache_config` from `__init__` (together with the block size check), and this line reads it. The two branches merge without a conflict, but the result fails `ruff` with F821 (undefined name `cache_config`), so whichever lands second breaks b12x init. Reading `vllm_config.cache_config.block_size` directly here keeps it working in either order.

+    above the b12x page sizes (e.g. 2176); the worker then splits each block
+    into kernel pages, so the backend must accept any multiple of them.

+    assert select_common_block_size(192, [B12xPagedAttentionBackend]) == 64
+    assert not B12xPagedAttentionBackend.supports_block_size(96)

     assert _max_page_table_width(4096, 128, 4096, False) == 32

+def _worker_kernel_block_table_width(
+    max_model_len: int, block_size: int, kernel_block_size: int
+) -> int:
+    """Row length of the block table the worker hands to ``forward()``: the
+    manager block table (``AttentionGroup.create_metadata_builders``), with
+    every entry expanded into ``block_size // kernel_block_size`` kernel pages.
+    """
+    width = get_block_table_width(cdiv(max_model_len, block_size), block_size)
+    return width * (block_size // kernel_block_size)

Together with #62265, this lets a non-hybrid model run with an explicit block size that is a multiple of 64 but not 64 or 128. Example: Qwen3-0.6B, `block_size=192`, `max_model_len=4096`. The worker block table is `ceil(4096/192) = 22` blocks, which expands to 66 entries of 64-token kernel pages, but `_max_page_table_width()` (L62) sizes the plans for `ceil(4096/64) = 64`, and the extra capacity is only added for hybrid models. `forward()` passes the full table, so FlashInfer's check should reject it (`page_table width must fit the prepared capacity: got 66, expected 1..64`).

Should we size the plans from the manager block expanded into kernel pages, or keep rejecting sizes other than 64/128 for non-hybrid models? A test that the expanded table fits the plan would cover it.

Thanks, good catch. Reproduced on the Spark with both PRs applied (Qwen3-0.6B, `--block-size 192`, `--max-model-len 4096`): the engine dies at the first forward with `page_table width=66 exceeds scratch capacity 64` from `_scratch.py:_validate_runtime_metadata_reference` (a different check than the decode-graph one, same cause).

I went with sizing the plans from the manager block. `_max_page_table_width()` now takes the manager block size and mirrors what the worker does in `AttentionGroup.create_metadata_builders`: `get_block_table_width(cdiv(max_model_len, block_size), block_size) * (block_size // page_size)`. When the block is not known yet (the platform applies `get_preferred_block_size()` after the model is built) or is not a multiple of the page, it sizes for whole pages as before. The hybrid slack is unchanged.

Reusing `get_block_table_width` also covers the worker's 128-token block-table alignment: with `--block-size 64 --max-model-len 4000` the worker passes 64 entries but the plans were sized for `cdiv(4000, 64) = 63`. That one is independent of the two PRs (block size 64 passes both checks) and fails without them too: `page_table width=64 exceeds scratch capacity 63`.

Tests: `test_b12x_attention_plan_capacity_fits_expanded_block_table` sweeps block sizes 64..2176 and model lengths 1000..40960 and asserts the expanded worker table fits the plan, plus the two examples above; the new tests fail without the fix. On the Spark: `--block-size 192` and `--block-size 64 --max-model-len 4000` now start, greedy outputs match the 128 default, and the full `tests/v1/attention/test_b12x.py` passes (67 passed).

The new line sits a dozen lines below the constructor check #62265 removes, so the two should merge cleanly in either order.

#62265 deletes `cache_config = vllm_config.cache_config` from `__init__` (together with the block size check), and this line reads it. The two branches merge without a conflict, but the result fails `ruff` with F821 (undefined name `cache_config`), so whichever lands second breaks b12x init. Reading `vllm_config.cache_config.block_size` directly here keeps it working in either order.

Deployment validation (SM120, hybrid attention/mamba) — the confirmation you asked for on #62320:

- **Model:** `Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B` (Qwen3.5-MoE — full-attention + GDN linear-attention layers, i.e. hybrid), NVFP4, TP=1, RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell SE (SM120)
- **Stack:** vLLM 0.32.0 + b12x 1.5.1 (the tag's `[b12x]` pin), full production flags: `--attention-backend b12x --linear-backend b12x --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 128 --enable-prefix-caching --max-model-len 262144 --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'`
- **Before this change:** startup fails with `ValueError: Aligned KV cache block size 2176 is not supported by attention backend(s): B12X` (#62320)
- **With this change:** the gate passes (`Setting attention block size to 2176`, no ValueError), b12x runs on 128-token kernel pages, and the full startup + check + 19-case functional bench pass (0 failures)

One caveat: our run additionally needed the `hasattr(binding.q, "fake_mode")` guard in b12x 1.5.1's paged-priming compile — the standalone wheel (what `vllm[b12x]` pins) predates that fix, which is on flashinfer `main` and in the FlashInfer 0.7.2 bundled b12x. It's a separate bug from this change (we carried the guard as a local image patch, version-pinned + fail-loud); tracked at flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6940.

So from our side: this change alone makes hybrid + b12x startable on 0.32.0 under the full production config (fp8 KV + MTP spec decode + prefix caching + chunked prefill, 2176 aligned block) — which goes beyond the PR's bf16 / DGX-Spark validation.

Thanks @mike2307, that's exactly the confirmation this needed: fp8 KV + MTP + prefix caching + chunked prefill on the 2176-token block, beyond what I could cover on the Spark. The fake_mode crash is in the standalone b12x 1.5.1 wheel and is tracked separately in #62984 / flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6940.

Thanks @waynehacking8, that closes the loop: same quality and decode throughput as the default backend on the 2176-token block, on hardware I can’t test. The 2176 vs 2112 difference is just each backend’s kernel alignment (128 for b12x, 16/32 for FlashInfer). The per-batch-size Triton compile in the b12x warmup is independent of this change (graph_replay metadata kernel with BATCH as a constexpr, driven by cutedsl_warmup over every capture size); I’ll check whether it’s tracked and file it if not.

@waynehacking8 filed the warmup compile issue you ran into as [flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#7030](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/7030), with your gist linked. It’s a tl.static_range(0, BATCH) in the b12x prefill metadata kernel, one unrolled compile per batch size; on my Spark a one-line range swap took the 128-seq warmup from 17 min to 19 s with identical outputs.

One thing my review left out: in the same runs b12x is slower to the first token. At c=1 the median TTFT is 90.1 ms against 79.2 ms for the default backend, over 16 requests each with a standard deviation of about 2 ms. At c=16 the medians (349.5 and 335.6 ms) differ by much less than the request-to-request spread (standard deviation 52 and 58 ms). The b12x server also needed 205 s to become ready against 140 s.

Both arms run this head with one boot each, so this compares the two backends, not the change. I've added these rows to the review table. Numbers: `P-b12x-c1.txt`, `P-def-c1.txt`, the two c=16 files and `job-log-run3.txt` in https://gist.github.com/waynehacking8/f77c201b8e02452ee5508a31162235bb

Thanks for adding those. Agreed it’s backend vs backend: this PR only lifts the block-size gate so b12x can start on hybrid models, and the hybrid split doesn’t touch the prefill path, so the c=1 TTFT gap is b12x’s own prefill cost on that card. Worth a separate look. The extra startup time is at least partly the per-batch warmup compile in [flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#7030](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/7030).

@LucasWilkinson @MatthewBonanni gentle ping on this one when you have a moment. It is a one-line change (drops the exact-size `supports_block_size` override so the worker's kernel-page split applies to b12x like the other backends), and since opening it has been confirmed independently on two SM120 setups above: mike2307 on Ornith-1.5-35B NVFP4 with fp8 KV, MTP and prefix caching, and waynehacking8 on Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-FP8 with GSM8K and TPOT matching the default FlashInfer path. Still applies cleanly to main. Happy to adjust if you would like it done differently.
